clue.text: Objection to hospital bill about cleaning equipment

indicators.note: about can mean turned around, so everything before it is read from the other end

blocks.note: a but is an objection, as in 'no buts'
H is the abbreviation for hospital
a tab is a bill run up at a bar

explanation.surface: Someone protests at the size of a hospital's invoice for its cleaning kit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'About' sits after the whole wordplay, so it turns everything before it, not just the bill.
explanation.definitionFit: A tub you wash yourself in counts, loosely, as a piece of washing gear for the home.

clue.text: It can be brought home and saved

definitions.text: It can be brought home and saved

blocks.note: surface reading: a thing carried back to the house, like shopping
setter's reading: two idioms, earning a living and being rescued from trouble, both name the same cured meat

explanation.surface: Something carried back to the house and then put by for later.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bring home the bacon' means earn a living, and 'save someone's bacon' means rescue them.
explanation.definitionFit: Both stock English idioms use this cured pork as their object, so the meat fits each phrase.

clue.text: Loudly denounce the most subordinate

indicators.note: most of a word means all but its final letter is kept

blocks.note: taken as written, then cut short
someone subordinate is under another

explanation.surface: Shouting angrily at whoever is lowest in the pecking order.
explanation.definitionFit: To thunder against something is to condemn it in a booming voice, a common figurative verb.

clue.text: Child-bearing system that's for the better

blocks.note: a tot is a small child
E, east, is a compass bearing

explanation.surface: A sling or carrier that makes having a baby easier.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Child-bearing' looks like one idea but splits into child and bearing; 'better' is one who bets.
explanation.definitionFit: The tote, short for totalisator, is the pool betting system run at racecourses for punters.

clue.text: Buffalo Bill show, "The West", goes public

indicators.note: to buffalo someone is to baffle them, so the words that follow are thrown into confusion

blocks.note: every letter of these four words is used

explanation.surface: Buffalo Bill's Wild West touring spectacle is put on for the public.
explanation.walkthrough: Buffalo Bill was a real showman, so 'Buffalo' hides inside his name.
explanation.definitionFit: Exposing wrongdoing to outsiders is the idiom of a whistleblower making secrets known openly.

clue.text: Volatile dictator forgetting one-time head supplier

indicators.note: forgetting something means leaving it out of the word
volatile means unstable, so the letters will not stay put

blocks.note: taken as written
one T, the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: A hot-tempered tyrant forgets about someone who used to be in charge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One-time' reads as former, but it means one letter T to drop from the dictator.
explanation.definitionFit: The carotid arteries in the neck carry blood up to the brain and face.

clue.text: One into talking exchanges vs one into making no changes

indicators.note: exchanges tells you two letters named next swap places with each other

blocks.note: someone keen on talk
the two letters V and S, which trade places

explanation.surface: The chatterbox and the stick-in-the-mud are set against each other.
explanation.walkthrough: 'vs' looks like versus, setting two people against each other; it is the letters V and S to swap in CONVERSATIONIST.
explanation.definitionFit: A conservationist works to preserve nature and heritage as they are, resisting alteration.

clue.text: Find out second time colour is spread

blocks.note: red is a colour
taken as written
a spread is a bed cover

explanation.surface: Discovering anew how paint is applied.
explanation.definitionFit: To come upon something again after losing or forgetting it is to learn of it once more.

clue.text: Three times English going for French - where's the problem?

indicators.note: one thing going for another means it is swapped out to make room

blocks.note: treble means three times as much
E is the abbreviation for English
où is French for where

explanation.surface: A puzzled query about a problem translating between English and French.
explanation.walkthrough: The first E of TREBLE is replaced by the French word for where.
explanation.definitionFit: Trouble is difficulty or a worry, so it can stand for a problem.

clue.text: Sweet twisted in strands

indicators.note: twisted round, the word is turned to face the other way

blocks.note: hair in tresses, long locks, is tressed

explanation.surface: A sugary treat like spun sugar twisted into strings.
explanation.definitionFit: A sweet is the British word for the pudding course served after the main meal.

clue.text: Stop at nothing

blocks.note: surface reading: be ruthless, do anything to get your way
setter's reading: a sequence of numbers that ends when it reaches zero

explanation.walkthrough: The idiom means be utterly ruthless, but read literally it describes a count that halts at zero, as before a rocket launch.
explanation.definitionFit: A launch sequence counts backwards and finishes when the numbers hit zero, the moment of lift-off.

clue.text: Refuse to bed down around king

indicators.note: around means the first part wraps about the second

blocks.note: to doss is British slang for to sleep rough
R, rex, is the abbreviation for king

explanation.surface: Someone declines to sleep near the monarch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Refuse' looks like a verb but is the noun, rubbish.
explanation.definitionFit: Dross is worthless waste matter, originally the scum on molten metal, so it is rubbish.

clue.text: Push lacking force is uncovered

indicators.note: lacking means something is missing from the word

blocks.note: a nudge is a small push
g is the symbol for gravitational force, as in g-force

explanation.surface: A weak shove leaves someone exposed.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone naked has no clothes over them, so they are bare and exposed.

clue.text: Nothing judicious takes time to be apparent

indicators.note: a word that takes something holds it inside itself

blocks.note: O looks like zero
judicious means showing good sense
T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: Wise judgement only becomes visible with time.
explanation.definitionFit: Ostensible describes what seems or is stated to be true on the surface, which is apparent in that sense.

clue.text: Fighting men taking first defensive measure

indicators.note: first means only the opening letter of the next word is used

blocks.note: a battle is fighting
taken as written
the opening letter of taking

explanation.surface: Soldiers taking the first step to defend themselves.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Measure' hints at an action, but here it is a structure: a notched parapet on a castle wall.
explanation.definitionFit: A battlement is the crenellated wall atop a fortress, built to protect its defenders.

clue.text: Shore split by river opening

indicators.note: something split by another word has that word pushed into its middle

blocks.note: a beach is a shore
R is the abbreviation for river

explanation.surface: A coastline cut through where a river reaches the sea.
explanation.definitionFit: A breach is a gap or hole broken through a wall or defence.

clue.text: Wild flower without name

indicators.note: without here means outside, so the first word goes around the second

blocks.note: a violet is a flower
N is the abbreviation for name

explanation.surface: An untamed bloom that nobody has named.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Without' reads as lacking, but it is the old sense outside.
explanation.definitionFit: Wild behaviour is unrestrained and forceful, close in meaning to violent.

clue.text: Amerindians step on ice

definitions.note: plural: the people as a group

blocks.note: first meaning: a Native American people of the south-eastern US
second meaning: a figure-skating turn from one foot to the other

explanation.surface: Native Americans walk carefully across a frozen lake.
explanation.definitionFit: The Choctaw are a Native American nation, and the name also labels a skating manoeuvre changing edge and direction.

clue.text: Will extra detectives turn up in wind?

indicators.note: in a down entry, turning up means reading from the bottom
in means placed inside the next word

blocks.note: to wind is to coil
CID is the British police Criminal Investigation Department

explanation.surface: Will more police officers show up despite the stormy weather?
explanation.walkthrough: 'Will' looks like the auxiliary verb opening a question but is the noun, a testament.
explanation.definitionFit: A codicil is a supplement added to a testament, amending or adding to its terms.

clue.text: Arranged for hospital worker

blocks.note: first meaning: neat, in good order
second meaning: an attendant doing non-medical ward tasks

explanation.surface: Something set up on behalf of a hospital employee.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective means tidily set out, and the noun names a ward attendant or porter.

clue.text: First the Left may finally score

indicators.note: first means only the opening letter of the following word counts
finally points to the closing letter of the word before it

blocks.note: the opening letter of the
left as a verb means departed, went
the closing letter of may

explanation.surface: A prediction that the political left will at last win something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Left' looks like the political wing, but it is the past tense of leave.
explanation.definitionFit: A score is an old word for a group of twenty, as in 'three score years and ten'.

clue.text: Crawler said to designate power

indicators.note: said means we go by how the words are spoken, not spelt

blocks.note: to term is to designate, and might is power

explanation.surface: A toady is described as giving someone authority.
explanation.walkthrough: TERM and MIGHT said together sound like the insect's name.
explanation.definitionFit: A termite is a small insect that creeps through wood, so it is a crawling creature.

clue.text: Instrument performed with dire effect in schmaltz

indicators.note: with effect suggests something worked on and changed, so the word before is rearranged
in means placed inside the next word

blocks.note: to perform is to do, past tense did
goo is sickly sentimentality, like schmaltz
the letters of dire rearranged

explanation.surface: A musician plays horribly, drowning the tune in sentimentality.
explanation.definitionFit: The didgeridoo is a long wooden wind instrument of Aboriginal Australia, producing a droning sound.

clue.text: Neat stall to copy

blocks.note: first meaning: a manger or stall for cattle, neat being an old word for cattle
second meaning: to cheat by copying someone else's work

explanation.surface: A tidy market stand set up to copy a rival.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Neat' looks like tidy, but it is the old word for cattle.
explanation.definitionFit: A crib is a stall or manger for oxen, and to crib is to copy dishonestly.

clue.text: Purchase involving  delivery of horse and  carriage

indicators.note: involving means holding something inside it

blocks.note: a buy is a purchase
gee-gee is how a small child pronounces horse, a nursery word

explanation.surface: Buying a horse and carriage on condition they are delivered.
explanation.definitionFit: A buggy is a light horse-drawn carriage, and in Britain also a pushchair.

clue.text: Peel's trick

blocks.note: first meaning: the outer layer of fruit
second meaning: to swindle someone out of money

explanation.surface: A trick performed by somebody named Peel, such as the Victorian prime minister.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Peel's' looks like a person's name; it is the fruit rind.
explanation.definitionFit: Peel is the outer rind of fruit, and to skin someone is slang for fleecing them.

clue.text: South in remedy for a 9 in Scotland

indicators.note: in means placed inside the following word

blocks.note: a cure is a remedy
S is the abbreviation for south

explanation.surface: A treatment for a southern Scottish ailment.
explanation.walkthrough: '9' looks like a cross-reference to 9 across, but it is a playing card.
explanation.definitionFit: The nine of diamonds is traditionally nicknamed the Curse of Scotland, so the card is called that there.

clue.text: First two of 2's clue second

blocks.note: the opening pair of letters of two, written as the numeral
an inkling is a hint or clue

explanation.surface: A cross-reference asking for the start of another clue's answer.
explanation.walkthrough: '2's clue' looks like a pointer to 2 down; it is the word two, then a hint.
explanation.definitionFit: In a twinkling means in an instant, so it is a very brief moment.

clue.text: Baby gear's still needed in the wee hours

indicators.note: in means placed inside the words that follow

blocks.note: the wee hours are very late at night
still and yet both mean even now

explanation.surface: Parents still need the baby things in the small hours of the night.
explanation.definitionFit: A layette is the full set of clothes and bedding prepared for a newborn.

clue.text: Forcing an entry into hiding place

indicators.note: forcing suggests breaking in roughly, so the letters are knocked about

blocks.note: both words used whole

explanation.surface: A burglar breaks into a secret hideout.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hiding place' suggests a hideout but means a place where hides are processed.
explanation.definitionFit: A tannery is a works where animal skins are cured into leather, a place for hides.
